subject: Pricing path & procurement: FinPay token volumes and who signs
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@finpay.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 08:22:00 +0000
Subject: Pricing path and procurement for FinPay token volumes

Thanks for the demo this morning — really helpful. A quick recap from our side and a couple of asks so we can move internally: 

- Expected usage profile: baseline ~150M tokens/month, with predictable spikes to ~350M tokens for quarter-end processing windows.
- Primary use: customer-facing summarization + reranking for payment exceptions.
- Budget guidance: we need to know a target $/1M tokens estimate so we can sense-check with finance. We're hoping to stay in the ballpark of €2,000–€3,000 per 1M tokens (rough range for initial planning).

What we need from Redwood to proceed:
1) A rough price band for 1M tokens (no formal quote yet) at the volumes above.
2) Who should we put on the procurement email chain (legal/PO path) — does Redwood send standard SOW/PO invoices or do we run through a vendor onboarding process?
3) Who at FinPay should be identified as the economic buyer (we'll confirm internally but I can introduce once you tell me the best contact/title to include).

If you can send a short note back with a price band + who we should put on the PO/finance thread, that would help accelerate our internal conversation.

Thanks,
Liam
Head of Product
FinPay

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@finpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 13:07:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Pricing path and procurement for FinPay token volumes

Thanks Liam — great to meet you and appreciate the clear numbers. Short answers below and a suggested next step.

1) Price band (preliminary, based on the volumes you shared):
   - Baseline / committed band (150M/mo steady): €1,400 – €2,100 per 1M tokens depending on commit length and retention/kv-cache settings.
   - Burst/peak handling (350M spikes): add-on burst units priced at a higher marginal rate; effective blended rate typically +10–30% depending on burst frequency.

   These are initial bands — we can firm up a binding price once we know commit term and billing cadence. I attached a short pricing sketch for reference.

2) Procurement path: we support both PO and credit-card-based onboarding. For enterprise contracts (recommended at your volumes) we generally run: Mutual NDA -> SOW/Order Form (DocuSign) -> PO + billing setup.

3) Economic buyer / finance sign-off: who ultimately signs off on the spend? If you can introduce the person who owns the cloud/AI budget (head of finance or controller) that will speed approval. We typically need finance for payment terms + procurement for onboarding.

Suggested next step: Can you introduce the finance contact and procurement lead? If you prefer, Marissa here can draft a compact mutual action plan and an early-stage order form to make the internal approval path clearer.

Thanks — I can be flexible on a quick 15–20m call if that helps.

—Karthik
VP, Partnerships & GTM
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_pricing_sketch_v1.xlsx (stub)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@finpay.com>, procurement@finpay.com
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 06 Oct 2026 09:15:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Pricing path and procurement for FinPay token volumes

Looping in procurement to make the PO path explicit. Hi procurement team — pleased to e-meet you.

Quick items from our side to help move to an internal PO: 
- I'll prepare a 1-page Mutual Action Plan (MAP) that maps approvals -> dates -> owners (draft attached).
- For contracting: we can accept standard FinPay PO terms; typical lead time for enterprise onboarding (legal + billing) is 7–14 business days once redlines are minimal.
- Please confirm: who is the signatory for contracts (Procurement Lead or CFO)? Also let us know preferred billing currency and whether a supplier questionnaire is required.

If it helps, we can include an estimated annual spend bucket based on the mid-point of Karthik's band. Example: 200M tokens/mo blended at €1,750 per 1M -> ~€4.2M ARR (ballpark to put on the PO).

Marissa
Sales Ops, Redwood Inference

Attachment: FinPay_Mutual_Action_Plan_DRAFT.pdf (stub)

From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@finpay.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Eve Barton <eve.barton@finpay.com>, procurement@finpay.com
Date: Tue, 06 Oct 2026 15:48:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Pricing path and procurement for FinPay token volumes

Thanks Karthik & Marissa — all helpful. Quick confirmations from our side: 

- Economic buyer: Eve Barton, Head of Finance (cc'd). She owns approvals for vendor spend above €250k.
- Procurement contact: procurement@finpay.com will manage vendor onboarding and the PO.
- Budget target: Eve has penciled in a target blended rate of ~€2,500 per 1M tokens for planning purposes (this sits in the middle of the band you provided). We have some runway to consider higher commit in exchange for a lower unit rate.
- Timeline: procurement + legal expect to complete vendor setup in ~2–3 weeks if we have a clean SOW.

Please go ahead and share the MAP + a non-binding order form (estimate) addressed to procurement@finpay.com and Eve. We will route internally and follow up with any required supplier documents.

Cheers,
Liam
Head of Product
FinPay
